new_packages.label: יִרְאָה, צֶדֶק וֶאֱמוּנָה
new_packages.label_en: Fear, Justice, and Faith — The Two Tiers of Awe
new_packages.reason: All five nodes in this cluster are different expressions of the same essential reality: the fear of God in its two tiers. The teaching opens by identifying two forms of fear (יִרְאַת הָעֹנֶשׁ and יִרְאַת הָרוֹמְמוּת) and immediately equates each with a second concept via נִקְרָא: fear of punishment IS justice (צֶדֶק); fear of exaltedness IS faith (אֱמוּנָה). Jacob (יַעֲקֹב) IS fear (יִרְאָה) — via the common root עָקֵב / יַעֲקֹב. These are not cause-and-effect; they are different names/faces of the same domain: the inner experience of holy awe. The Zohar passage at the end confirms the unity: צֶדֶק and אֱמוּנָה are the same quality at two stages of development ('before אֱמֶת joins' vs. 'after אֱמֶת joins'). The teaching's thesis is that both tiers of fear are necessary and that the lower (צֶדֶק) is the pathway into the higher (אֱמוּנָה) — but the NATURE of the cluster is: expressions of God-fearing consciousness.

new_packages.note_on_יראה: The node יִרְאָה (fear, general) serves as the hub linking יַעֲקֹב to both יִרְאַת הָעֹנֶשׁ and יִרְאַת הָרוֹמְמוּת. If added as a node, it would increase the cluster to 6 nodes. The source text uses it freely as the general category (line 5: 'צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת לוֹ יִרְאָה, הַנִּקְרָא צֶדֶק'; line 7: 'יַעֲקֹב הוּא יִרְאָה').
new_packages.evil_mirror: None. This Torah has no explicit evil mirror. The 'evil' element in the teaching (the דִּינִים — judgments that are aroused against someone walking the straight path) is not given an independent bechina cluster; it appears only as an eitza consequence of צֶדֶק ('וְהוּא יִשְׁפֹּט תֵּבֵל בְּצֶדֶק — לְפִיכָךְ מִתְעוֹרְרִין עָלָיו הַדִּינִים'). The teaching's structure is entirely within the good domain.

new_packages.label: אַבְרָהָם וּדְבֵקוּת
new_packages.label_en: Abraham and Cleaving — The Nature of Lovingkindness
new_packages.reason: Abraham (אַבְרָהָם) is explicitly equated with cleaving to God (דְּבֵקוּת) via the bechina marker נִקְרָא: 'אַבְרָהָם נִקְרָא מִי שֶׁבָּא לְדַבֵּק אֶת עַצְמוֹ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ'. The etymology provided — from the phrase אָבוֹא רָם ('I will come to the Exalted') — links the name Abraham to the act of approaching and cleaving to God. In the verse, חֶסֶד (lovingkindness) is the quality associated with Abraham, and the teaching implies that חֶסֶד flows naturally from the cleaving-nature. This is the destination-cluster: once the fear-cluster (Package A) attains אֱמֶת/אֱמוּנָה, the חֶסֶד/Abraham quality follows. The connection between the two clusters is eitza (not bechina).

new_packages.note_on_size: This is a 2-node cluster. Under the algorithm, 2-node clusters are candidates for merger into a larger component. However, there is no larger component in this Torah into which it can be merged via bechina (the connection from Package A to Package B is an eitza, not a bechina). It stands as a small but independently justified package, similar to Torah #82 Package 3 (שלהבת י"ה / מים חמין).

observations:
Torah #87 is a short teaching (9 lines) structured entirely around bechina equalities and a single eitza chain, yet none of the bechina edges are currently in the dataset. The teaching's conceptual structure is clear and tight:

1. STRUCTURE: Two tiers of fear are named and equated with two concepts (צֶדֶק and אֱמוּנָה). Jacob represents fear. Abraham represents cleaving. The verse 'תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב חֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם' is decoded as: give the higher fear (truth/faith) to the fear-cluster (Jacob), and then lovingkindness will come to the cleaving-cluster (Abraham).

2. BECHINA LANGUAGE: The text uses נִקְרָא and הוּא extensively — 5 explicit bechina equations in 9 lines. The framework (section 1.1) explicitly lists נִקְרָא as a canonical bechina marker ('X נקרא Y — X is called Y').

3. WHY NO CURRENT PACKAGES: The dataset contains only one edge for this Torah (id 297, eitza), capturing only the causal flow. The 5–6 bechina equalities that form the scaffolding of the teaching are missing. This is a data gap, not a structural absence.

4. CRITERION MET FOR NEW_PACKAGES_PROPOSED: Package A has 5 concepts (יראת העונש, צדק, יראת הרוממות, אמונה, יעקב) connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent conceptual domain (the domain of holy fear / God-consciousness). This exceeds the threshold of 3+ concepts.

5. EITZA CHAIN (already in dataset): יִרְאַת הָעֹנֶשׁ → אֱמוּנָה (edge id 297) correctly represents the causal flow within Package A: the lower tier leads to the higher tier. This is also the inter-package flow: Package A (at its highest node, אֱמוּנָה) produces the Package B outcome (חֶסֶד flows to Abraham/cleaving).

6. THE ZOHAR INTEGRATION (line 9): The closing Zohar quote from Parashat Balak confirms the package structure from the Kabbalistic side: צֶדֶק (justice, fear of punishment) is the unattached quality; when אֱמֶת (truth, the higher fear) joins it, it becomes אֱמוּנָה. This reinforces that צֶדֶק and אֱמוּנָה are the same underlying divine quality (the Shekhinah / Malkhut) at two stages — a classic bechina structure.
